headings.text: How your product shows up in the UI

blocks.html:
Integrating a product means building a small HTTP service — a product integration API — that the core RASENMAEHER API (rmapi) can drive over mTLS, and that supplies the UI content and access users need to onboard to your product directly from the Deploy App UI.

What you are building

The core RASENMAEHER API (rmapi, repo pvarki/python-rasenmaeher-api) owns user identity and the device-certificate lifecycle. It is the point of integration: it calls out to your service whenever a user changes state, and it proxies your product card/UI to end users.

Your product integration API is a separate FastAPI service (commonly named <short_name>rmapi). It does two things:

  1. Receives user-lifecycle callbacks from the core rmapi over mTLS and reflects each event into your product (create accounts, revoke access, grant/remove admin rights, etc.).
  2. Describes itself to the Deploy App UI so a product card appears, and exposes the UI content/access the user needs.

Terminology — do not confuse these:

  • rmapi (core) = the central RASENMAEHER API. Handles main user CRUD and Deploy App operations. You do not build this; you integrate with it.
  • product integration API (a.k.a. product-rm integration API) = the service you build. Real examples: pvarki/python-matrix-rmapi (Matrix), pvarki/python-tak-rmapi (TAK), pvarki/python-mediamtx-rmmtxauthz (MediaMTX).

The callback contract

The core rmapi calls a fixed set of endpoints on your service. In the scaffold these live in src/<package>/api/usercrud.py:

Method & path When the core rmapi calls it
POST /api/v1/users/created A new user (device certificate) was created
POST /api/v1/users/revoked A user's device certificate was revoked
POST /api/v1/users/promoted A user was promoted to admin
POST /api/v1/users/demoted A user was demoted from admin
PUT /api/v1/users/updated A user's callsign was updated

Each handler receives a UserCRUDRequest (uuid, callsign, x509cert) and returns OperationResultResponse(success=...). You implement the events your product cares about and acknowledge the rest with return OperationResultResponse(success=True).

Authentication: mTLS, CN-pinned

Every lifecycle call must come from the core rmapi. The scaffold guards each endpoint with MTLSHeader and a comes_from_rm() check that compares the client-certificate CN against manifest["rasenmaeher"]["certcn"] (read from the deployment manifest at /pvarki/kraftwerk-init.json). Any other caller gets 403 Forbidden.

How your product shows up in the UI

Your service also serves a GET /api/v2/description/{language} endpoint that returns a ProductDescriptionExtended with a ProductComponent. The component type decides how the product card behaves:

  • **link** — the card opens an external URL.
  • **markdown** — the card opens inline per-user Markdown, served by your service and proxied by the core rmapi.
  • **component** — the card mounts a Module Federation React bundle built from your ui/ folder.

Where to start

  • Scaffold from the template — generate a working skeleton from pvarki/python-integration-template.
  • Worked example: Matrix — read a complete, production integration end to end.
  • Integration conventions & don'ts — the durable checklist before you ship.

Then follow the stack-specific setup pages: Set up your dev environment (Docker Compose) / (Kubernetes) and Register your integration (Docker Compose) / (Kubernetes).
